source_decisions: Printed footer establishes Spring 2008; the mixed-year compilation is never treated as one exam.
Q2 printed output gates are OR and AND with no output bubbles. O0 is steady constant 1; preserve the original physical network and distinguish physical path arc sums from sensitizable edges.

Q2 balanced numerical mean delays require Rp = Rn. General Rp/Rn formulas are included because Q2 does not state a mobility ratio. Dual-Vt selection is conditional on quantified slack and is not a unique global optimum.
Q3 uses the printed eta = (PT-PL)/PT, an intermediate-load overhead fraction. Integer N and recomputed beta preserve the actual load.
Q4 brackets the first two of three inverters. Alpha = 1 and 2 both meet T = 6RC; alpha = 1 minimizes the modeled switching power.
Q5 is a forward full adder. The printed final row is 111 -> s = 1, co = 1; the photo circle is annotation. The graded booklet instead solves an inverse relation and is corrected.
Q5 prints (10%), while the preceding questions total 90 points. Preserve the percentage mark and interpret it as the remaining ten points only for the coverage total.

semantic_conditions: The archive year is not printed, but all seven questions are covered by the six original panels.
Q1(h): mobility and threshold ratios are not provided. Use the general current-matching equation without inventing a two-times width.
Q2: complete final ON-graph first moments include attached opposite-network capacitors. The full-level constant-R model is declared; a 10–90 conversion is a one-pole estimate.
Q2: alpha01 means charging probability; activity counting both edges needs a factor of one-half. Internal nodes only.
Q3: high-Vt delay penalties and leakage weights are absent. The 24-MOS candidate has conditional 12L/12H marking and explicit slack bounds, with no unconditional optimum or speed guarantee.
Q4: constant threshold is 0.4 V. Body-effect parameters are absent; qualitative levels are not measured dynamic waveforms.
Q5: exactly 8RC; alpha=1 and 3 are feasible, and 1 minimizes modeled power. The first-two-stage bracket excludes the third external load.
Q6: conventional single complementary-gate XOR uses 12 MOS; broader static TG XOR uses 8. Style and minimum scope are explicit.
Q7: the complete 28-MOS implementation uses only true primary inputs; the reference omits complement generators.
